planting.note: Plant bulb or container stock in spring in full sun in well-drained, lean, sandy to rocky, alkaline soil; Spice Lily is a Texas and northern Mexico native prized for heavily maroon-spotted foliage and clove-scented evening flowers.

directions: Plant in well-drained, lean, sandy to rocky, alkaline soil in full sun; Spice Lily is highly drought tolerant once established and rots quickly in heavy or poorly drained soil. Native to limestone hills and rocky prairies of Texas and northern Mexico, this low, clumping succulent-leaved perennial produces flat rosettes of gray-green foliage densely marked with maroon-purple spots, giving it strong ornamental appeal even out of bloom. In summer, tall, slender flower spikes rise well above the foliage bearing tubular, greenish to purple-brown flowers that open at dusk with a spicy, clove-like fragrance, drawing hawk moths and hummingbirds. Unlike true agaves it blooms repeatedly without dying, making it a reliable long-term xeric garden accent for rock gardens and gravel beds.

common_name: Cow's Tongue Prickly Pear (Texas Native Spineless-Type Prickly Pear)

planting.note: Plant rooted pads in spring in full sun in very well-drained, sandy to rocky, alkaline soil; Opuntia cacanapa is a Texas and northern Mexico native prickly pear and the parent species of the widely grown near-spineless 'Ellisiana' cultivar.

directions: Root pads in well-drained, sandy to rocky, alkaline soil in full sun; let cut pads callus for a few days before planting to prevent rot. Native to South Texas and northern Mexico, this large, mounding prickly pear bears broad, elongated pads that give rise to its common name, along with bright yellow spring flowers and edible reddish-purple fruit later in the season. It is the source species behind the popular near-spineless 'Ellisiana' cultivar widely planted for livestock forage and low-maintenance landscaping, though the straight species typically carries more spines than that selection. Extremely drought tolerant once established, it needs no supplemental water beyond rainfall in most of its hardiness range and should never be planted in heavy or poorly drained soil, which quickly causes pad rot.
